title: New Tools for Determining Challenging Structures by Cryo-EM
content: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has revolutionized structural biology, yet challenges persist for many samples. Tubular biological specimens often exhibit locally ordered, rather than globally helical, lattices and variations in diameter, complicating structural determination. Globular particles frequently exhibit preferred orientations and deleterious interactions with the air–water interface, limiting high-resolution reconstructions. To address these issues, we have developed two complementary approaches: reconstruction of average subtracted tubular regions (RASTR) for determining structures of challenging tubular biological molecules and specimen preparation on a tube—RASTR (SPOT-RASTR) for optimizing specimen preparation of globular particles. Here, we present new developments and advances using these methodologies.
